Subject: Redwood inference - Procurement & pricing next steps

Hi Sophie / Mark —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so procurement has what they need: 

Summary of call:
- Use case: Acme will evaluate Redwood for customer-facing document summarization and routing; expected steady-state usage ~500M tokens/month across dev and prod.
- Primary requirement: predictable latency and cost; regulation requires contract + audit evidence (SOC2) and clear billing flow.
- Procurement preference: Sophie mentioned PO-based billing is likely, but card is acceptable for POC.
- Marketplace interest: you asked whether we support a marketplace (e.g., AWS Marketplace) to simplify purchase.

What I attached: Redwood_Quote_20260210.pdf (ballpark pricing / packaging for hosted / dedicated / private), SOC2-Summary.pdf (one-pager), SOW_Redwood-Acme-draft.docx (work-in-progress).

Next steps / asks:
1) Can you confirm procurement’s preferred payment method (PO + invoice vs corporate card) and any required PO terms (net30/net45, specific legal clauses)?
2) Confirm target procurement timeline and approver so we can align pricing and contract cadence.
3) Would you like a short 30-minute procurement-only call to run through the PO path + marketplace option?

Notes on packaging (high-level):
- Hosted (on-demand): fastest to start, card-friendly, on-demand billing. PO via invoicing also supported but typically with minimal commit.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): recommended if you want predictable throughput; generally requires a monthly or annual commit (we provide commit discounts).
- Private (VPC / on-prem): for regulated workloads; pricing is license + support; procurement/legal usually treats as a different paper process.

I’ve cc’d Aditya to flag any technical/compliance clarifications.

Thanks — I’ll wait on confirmation of payment method and timeline and can schedule the procurement sync once you’ve confirmed availability.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick answers from procurement’s side: 

- Payment method: our standard is PO + invoice (net30). For pilots we can do a corporate card but anything above $10k/mo will need a PO.
- Marketplace: yes, AWS Marketplace would be ideal for us if that supports PO billing and aligns with our legal. Is Redwood available there?
- Commit vs on-demand: procurement prefers commits if there’s a discount and it simplifies budget planning. Can you send the commit tiers and typical minimums?
- Security: we’ll need SOC2 report and an owner-level contact for security questions. Also please confirm data retention & encryption (KMS) details.

Can we do a short procurement call Thursday morning my time to confirm PO flow and who signs? I’ve looped Mark (IT procurement) and procurement@acme.com.

Thanks,
Sophie
Head of Vendor Procurement | Acme Corp

Thanks Sophie — great questions. Below are concise answers to help procurement and finance evaluate options; happy to walk through on a quick call.

Payment / billing flow:
- PO + invoice (net30) is supported for Hosted and Dedicated. We generate monthly invoices tied to the billing account once PO is in place.
- Corporate card is supported for POC / short-term pilots; we can process cards through our payments partner.
- AWS Marketplace: yes — we do support AWS Marketplace procurement which can simplify PO and marketplace contract flow. I’ll confirm whether the specific SKU you’ll use is listed; Marketplace can often speed procurement approvals.

Packaging & commit guidance (ballpark):
- Hosted (on-demand): no committed spend required. Recommended for initial POC. Example: list pricing ~ $0.0008 / token (example only).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): requires a commit — typical structures: 6-month commit (approx 10% discount), 12-month commit (approx 20% discount) on top of reduced unit pricing; minimums vary by capacity (we can model to your 500M tokens/month). Dedicated provides predictable latency and cost.
- Private deployment (VPC / on-prem): available for regulated data — generally procured via enterprise contract with a platform license + support fee; often a different procurement and legal track.

Security & compliance:
- SOC2: attached SOC2-Summary.pdf; we can provide the full report under an NDA.
- Encryption: supports customer-managed KMS in Dedicated and Private; hosted supports encryption at rest and in transit.

Requested docs I attached: Redwood_Quote_20260210.pdf (three packaging options with ballpark numbers), SOW_Redwood-Acme-draft.docx (draft).

Proposed next steps:
1) If PO is the path, please share procurement contact + template PO terms (or a sample PO header) so we can map to our billing.
2) If marketplace is preferred, let me know and I’ll confirm SKU availability & provide marketplace purchase flow.
3) Suggest a 30-minute procurement sync — I’m available Thu 11:00–12:30 PT.

If it helps, Aditya (cc’d) can provide a one-page procurement checklist (paper, security docs, billing flow) and Dev (cc’d) can answer KMS/encryption specifics live on the call.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: Redwood_Quote_20260210.pdf, SOC2-Summary.pdf, SOW_Redwood-Acme-draft.docx

Quick note from the infra/compliance side — happy to join the procurement call. A couple of items procurement typically asks for that we can prepare in advance: 

- One-page procurement checklist (paper route, PO header, invoicing contact, billing cadence) — I’ll share a template before the call.
- SOC2 report availability: we can provide under NDA within 24–48 hours.
- KMS details: for Dedicated and Private we can use customer-managed KMS; hosted supports envelope encryption with our managed keys and can integrate with customer KMS for dedicated flows.
- Marketplace flow: AWS Marketplace usually supports PO but depends on procurement setup; Marketplace purchases often map to a single billing contract and simplify renewals.

If you confirm Thu 11:00 PT works, I’ll drop the procurement checklist and a brief slide summarizing commit tiers (6/12 months) and expected billing flows.
